causes.label: Dryer is unplugged
remedies: Make sure the dryer plug is pushed completely into the outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Dryer is unplugged"

causes.label: Fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped
remedies: Check the building’s fuse/circuit breaker box and replace fuse or reset breaker.
NOTE: Electric dryers use two fuses/breakers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped"

causes.label: Thermal limiter tripped
remedies: Check the vent for any obstructions.
Call authorized service person for replacement, if necessary.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Thermal limiter tripped"

causes.label: Fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped, the dryer may tumble but not heat
remedies: Check the building’s fuse/circuit breaker box and replace fuse or reset breaker.
Your dryer may tumble if only one fuse is blown or one breaker tripped.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped, the dryer may tumble but not heat"

causes.label: Gas service is off
remedies: Make sure gas shutoff at dryer and main shutoff are fully open.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Gas service is off"

causes.label: LP gas supply tank is empty or there has been a utility interruption of natural gas (gas models)
remedies: Refill or replace tank.
Dryer should heat when utility service is restored.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "LP gas supply tank is empty or there has been a utility interruption of natural gas (gas models)"

causes.label: Some shaking/noise is normal. Dryer may be sitting unevenly
remedies: Move dryer to an even floor space, or adjust leveling legs as necessary until even.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Some shaking/noise is normal. Dryer may be sitting unevenly"

causes.label: Improper use of fabric softener
remedies: Follow directions on fabric softener package.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Improper use of fabric softener"

causes.label: Lint filter is full
remedies: Clean lint screen before each load.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Lint filter is full"

causes.label: Improper sorting
remedies: Sort lint producers (like chenille) from lint collectors (like corduroy).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Improper sorting"

causes.label: Static electricity can attract lint
remedies: See suggestions in this section under STATIC.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Static electricity can attract lint"

causes.label: Overloading
remedies: Separate large loads into smaller ones.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Overloading"

causes.label: Overdrying
remedies: Try a fabric softener.
Adjust controls for less drying.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Overdrying"

causes.label: No fabric softener was used
remedies: Try a fabric softener.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "No fabric softener was used"

causes.label: Synthetics, permanent press and blends can cause static
remedies: Try a fabric softener.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Synthetics, permanent press and blends can cause static"

causes.label: Type of heat
remedies: Automatic drying times will vary according to the type of heat used (electric, natural or LP gas), size of load, types of fabrics, wetness of clothes and condition of exhaust ducts.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Type of heat"

symptoms.symptom: Clothes take too long to dry

causes.label: Improper sorting
remedies: Separate heavy items from lightweight items (generally, a well-sorted washer load is a well-sorted dryer load).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Improper sorting"

causes.label: Overdrying
remedies: Select a shorter drying time.
Remove items while they still hold a slight amount of moisture.
Select a LESS DRY setting.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Overdrying"

causes.label: Letting items sit in dryer after cycle ends
remedies: Remove items when cycle ends and fold or hang immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Letting items sit in dryer after cycle ends"

causes.label: Overloading
remedies: Separate large loads into smaller ones.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Overloading"
